classification.difficultyReason: Construct a proof of the centre-on-arm case using equal radii and an exterior angle.

content.prompt:
Suppose the centre of the circle is on the inscribed angle.

Prove that the central angle is double the measure of the inscribed angle. Hint: Find an isosceles triangle.

spec.description: Vertical diameter through O, with a lower-left circumference point joined to the top endpoint and centre.
spec.mathematics: The centre lies on one arm of the inscribed angle; the central angle uses the lower diameter endpoint.
spec.answerVisibility: Only O is labelled in the question. Proof labels and equal angles appear in the solution only.

answer.short:
$\angle AOC=2\angle ABC$.

Equal radii give equal base angles; the central angle is their exterior angle.
answer.worked:
Label the top and bottom diameter endpoints $B$ and $C$, and the lower-left point $A$. Since $OA=OB$, $\triangle AOB$ is isosceles. Let $\angle OAB=\angle OBA=\alpha$.

As $B$, $O$ and $C$ are collinear, $\angle AOC$ is an exterior angle of $\triangle AOB$:
$$\begin{align*}\angle AOC&=\angle OAB+\angle OBA\\\angle AOC&=2\alpha.\end{align*}$$
Since $\angle ABC=\angle ABO=\alpha$, $\angle AOC=2\angle ABC$.

spec.description: Complete proof figure with B at the top, C at the bottom, A lower-left, and equal base angles alpha.
spec.mathematics: OA=OB; angles OAB and OBA are alpha; BOC is a diameter.
spec.answerVisibility: Solution-only point labels and equal-angle annotations.
